text:
The pressure acting on a submarine is 3 $\times$ $10^{5} Pa$ at a certain depth. If the depth is doubled, the percentage increase in the pressure acting on the submarine would be : 

(Assume that atmospheric pressure is 1 $\times$ $10^{5} Pa$ and density of water is $10^{3} kg m^{-3}, g = 10 ms^{-2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$P = P_{0} + hρ$g = 3 $\times$ $10^{5} Pa$

$\Rightarrow$ h$ρ$g = 3 $\times$ $10^{5}$ $-$ 1 $\times$ $10^{5}$

$\Rightarrow$ h$ρ$g = 2 $\times$ $10^{5}$

$\therefore$ 2h$ρ$g = 4 $\times$ $10^{5}$

$\therefore$ $P' = P_{0} + 4$ $\times$ $10^{5}$

$\therefore$ P' = 5 $\times$ $10^{5} Pa$

$\therefore$ % increase in pressure = $\frac{P^{'}-P}{P}\times 100$

$=\frac{(5-3)\times 10^{5}}{3\times 10^{5}}\times 100$

$=\frac{200}{3}$%
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift

text: Time period of a simple pendulum is T inside a lift when the lift is stationary. If the lift moves upwards with an acceleration g/2, the time period of pendulum will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When lift is stationary

$T=2π\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$

A pseudo force will act downwards when lift is moving upwards.

$\therefore$ $g_{eff}=g+\frac{g}{2}=\frac{3g}{2}$

$\therefore$ New time period

$T^{'}=2π\sqrt{\frac{L}{g_{eff}}}$

$T^{'}=2π\sqrt{\frac{2L}{3g}}$

$\therefore$ $T^{'}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}T$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift

text:
Four equal masses, m each are placed at the corners of a square of length (l) as shown in the figure. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis passing through A and parallel to DB would be :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$AC=\sqrt{l^{2}+l^{2}}$

$AC=l\sqrt{2}$

$d=\frac{l\sqrt{2}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow d=\frac{l}{\sqrt{2}}$

Moment of inertia about the axis passing through A :

$I=m(O)^{2}+m(d)^{2}+m(d)^{2}+m(AC)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow I=O+m\left (\frac{l}{\sqrt{2}}\right )^{2}+m\left (\frac{l}{\sqrt{2}}\right )^{2}+m\left (l\sqrt{2}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow I=\frac{ml^{2}}{2}+\frac{ml^{2}}{2}+2ml^{2}$

$\Rightarrow I=3ml^{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift

text: The maximum and minimum distances of a comet from the Sun are 1.6 $\times$ $10^{12} m$ and 8.0 $\times$ $10^{10} m$ respectively. If the speed of the comet at the nearest point is 6 $\times$ $10^{4} ms^{-1}$, the speed at the farthest point is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$v_{1} = 6$ $\times$ $10^{4} m/s$

Let point 1 is nearest point,

and point 2 is farthest point.

Given, $r_{1} = 8$ $\times$ $10^{10} m$ & $r_{2} = 1.6$ $\times$ $10^{12} m$

By angular momentum conservation

$L_{1} = L_{2}$

$mr_{1}v_{1} = mr_{2}v_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{2} =$ $\frac{r_{1}v_{1}}{r_{2}}$

$\therefore$ $v_{2} =$ $\frac{8\times 10^{10}\times 6\times 10^{4}}{1.6\times 10^{12}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{2} = 3.0$ $\times$ $10^{3} m/s$

text:
A conducting wire of length 'l', area of cross-section A and electric resistivity $ρ$ is connected between the terminals of a battery. A potential difference V is developed between its ends, causing an electric current.

If the length of the wire of the same material is doubled and the area of cross-section is halved, the resultant current would be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know that

$R=ρ\frac{l}{A}$

Now, new length : $l^{'}=2l$

new area of cross section : $A^{'}=A/2$

$\therefore$ New resistance : $R^{'}=ρ.\frac{2l}{A/2}$

$\Rightarrow R^{'}=4\frac{ρl}{A}$

$\Rightarrow R^{'}=4R$

$\therefore$ Resultant current : $I=\frac{V}{4R}$

$\Rightarrow$ $I=\frac{1}{4}\frac{VA}{ρl}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift

text: One main scale division of a vernier callipers is 'a' cm and $n^{th}$ division of the vernier scale coincide with (n $-$ $1)^{th}$ division of the main scale. The least count of the callipers in mm is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
n VSD = (n $-$ 1) MSD

1 VSD = $\left (\frac{n-1}{n}\right )$MSD

L.C. = 1 MSD $-$ 1 VSD

= 1 MSD $-$ $\left (\frac{n-1}{n}\right )$MSD

= 1 MSD $-$ 1 MSD + $\frac{MSD}{n}$

= $\frac{MSD}{n}$

= $\frac{a}{n}$ cm

= $\frac{10a}{n}$ mm

text: The volume V of an enclosure contains a mixture of three gases, 16 g of oxygen, 28 g of nitrogen and 44 g of carbon dioxide at absolute temperature T. Consider R as universal gas constant. The pressure of the mixture of gases is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
No. of moles of $O_{2}$ : 

$n_{1} =$ $\frac{16}{32}$ = 0.5 mole

No. of moles of $N_{2}$ : 

$n_{2} =$ $\frac{28}{28}$ = 1 mole

No. of moles of $CO_{2}$ : 

$n_{3} =$ $\frac{44}{44}$ = 1 mole

Total no. of moles in container : $n = n_{1} + n_{2} + n_{3}$

$\therefore$ n = 0.5 + 1 + 1 = $\frac{5}{2}$ moles

Now; PV = nRT

$\Rightarrow$ P = $\frac{nRT}{V}$

$\Rightarrow$ P = $\frac{5}{2}\frac{RT}{V}$

text:
Consider a 20 kg uniform circular disk of radius 0.2 m. It is pin supported at its center and is at rest initially. The disk is acted upon by a constant force F = 20 N through a massless string wrapped around its periphery as shown in the figure.


[IMG]

Suppose the disk makes n number of revolutions to attain an angular speed of 50 rad $s^{-1}$.

The value of n, to the nearest integer, is $__________$.

[Given : In one complete revolution, the disk rotates by 6.28 rad]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$α=\frac{τ}{I}=\frac{F.R.}{mR^{2}/2}=\frac{2F}{mR}$

$α=\frac{2\times 20}{20\times (0.2)}=10$ rad$/s^{2}$

$ω^{2}=ω_{0}^{2}+2α\Delta θ$

$(50)^{2}=0^{2}+2(10)\Delta θ$

$\Rightarrow \Delta θ=\frac{2500}{20}$

$\Delta θ=125$ rad

No. of revolution $=\frac{125}{2π}\approx 20$ revolution
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift
